body.statement: On the restricted schedule class \(Y_i(2)=Y_i(3)\) for every \(i\), pool assignment labels \(2\) and \(3\). Under \(q^\star\), the resulting observation has balanced two-arm assignment, the target becomes \(n^{-1}\sum_i\{Y_i(1)-Y_i(2)\}\), and the exact orbit likelihood reduces to the shifted-binomial experiment of Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Theorem 2.1). Its restricted-class second-order constant is \(-4^{1/3}a_1'\), providing the required two-arm sanity reduction without asserting that this restricted constant equals \(C_3\).
body.justification: The reduction verifies the normalization and distinguishes the new worst-case three-arm geometry from an embedded two-arm submodel.
body.gap: The published scalar experiment supplies the known special case but does not establish how the unrestricted eight-type adversary lowers the constant to \(C_3\).
body.consumer: The identity provides a regression test for symbolic and numerical implementations of the eight-type likelihood.
body.proof_tex:
Assume \(Y_i(2)=Y_i(3)\) for every labelled unit and denote their common value by \(Y_i(0)\).  Under \(q^\star\),
\[
\Pr(A_i=1)=\frac12,\qquad
\Pr(A_i\in\{2,3\})=\frac12.
\]
After mapping both labels \(2,3\) to the pooled label \(0\), assignments are therefore iid balanced two-arm assignments.  Conditional on the pooled label, the distinction between \(2\) and \(3\) is ancillary because the two potential outcomes coincide.  Moreover
\[
\tau(z)=\frac1n\sum_i
\left\{Y_i(1)-\frac{Y_i(2)+Y_i(3)}2\right\}
=\frac1n\sum_i\{Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)\}.
\]

In the exact orbit likelihood, summing over every split \(r_2+r_3=r_0\) and the corresponding latent-table columns leaves precisely the hypergeometric count of assignments to the pooled arm.  The cited balanced two-arm reduction identifies this invariant kernel with the shifted-binomial experiment.  Applying the cited sharp theorem in its stated normalization gives the restricted-class second-order constant \(-4^{1/3}a_1'\).  Since \(C_3=-a_1'\), these constants are distinct; the calculation is only a restricted-submodel sanity check and makes no equality claim for the unrestricted eight-type game.
